cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, is having the house of the LORD repaired. While they're bringing out the money that had been taken into the house, Hilkiah the priest finds something. And friend, it is NOT loose change.

cards.question: While the money is being brought out of the house of the LORD, what does Hilkiah the priest find?
Hilkiah has found the Book of the Law of the LORD, given by ___.

cards.text: Hilkiah tells Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD!" and hands it over. Baker, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer waiting for somebody to find me, so give me a second, I'm getting misty.
Shaphan takes the book to the king. But before he says one word about it, he gives a report on the temple work.

cards.question: Shaphan brings the book to King Josiah but starts with a report on the temple work. What does he report?

answers.text: The money was paid to the supervisors and workers
The repairs on the house are all finished now
The money for the repairs has all run out

cards.text: Then he finally gets to it: "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." Friend, the man was HOLDING the Book of the Law, and he opened with the budget report!

cards.question: Shaphan reads the book in the presence of King Josiah.
When King Josiah hears the words of the Law, he ___ his clothes.

cards.text: Then Josiah gives an order to five men: Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant.

cards.question: King Josiah sends Hilkiah, Shaphan and three others out with an order. What does he tell them to do?

answers.text: Inquire of the LORD about the book
Make copies of the book for every city
Hide the book where it will be safe

cards.question: Josiah asks the men to inquire of the LORD only for himself.
Josiah says great is the wrath of the LORD poured out on them. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Their fathers did not keep the LORD's word
The temple was left in ruins for years
The people stopped giving to the temple

cards.text: So Hilkiah and the men the king picked head out to inquire of the LORD, just like Josiah told them. They go to someone who speaks for the LORD.

cards.question: Hilkiah and the king's men go to inquire of the LORD. Who do they go to?

cards.text: Huldah is the wife of Shallum, and she lives in Jerusalem, in the Second District. She answers the king's men with a message from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: Through Huldah, the LORD says He is about to bring ___ on this place and on its people.
The LORD says the calamity will come according to the curses written in the book read before the king.
Why does the LORD say calamity is coming on this place and its people?

answers.text: They forsook Him and burned incense to other gods
They let His house fall apart for many years
They lost the Book of the Law He had given

cards.text: Then the LORD says through Huldah, "My wrath will be poured out upon this place and will not be quenched." But the message isn't over yet, because next it turns to the king of Judah himself.

cards.question: The LORD says King Josiah's heart was ___ and he humbled himself when he heard God's words.
The LORD tells Josiah He has heard him, because Josiah tore his clothes and wept before Him.
Because Josiah humbled himself, what does the LORD promise him?

answers.text: His eyes won't see the coming calamity
The coming calamity will be called off
His kingdom will stand strong forever

cards.text: They bring Huldah's answer back, and Josiah summons all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem. Baker, if somebody told me "you personally are fine," I'd be napping next to the oven before the timer went off.

cards.question: King Josiah goes up to the house of the LORD with all the people, great and small. What does he do there?

answers.text: He reads them all the words of the book
He offers a great sacrifice to the LORD
He crowns his son as the next king

cards.question: The book Josiah reads to all the people is called the Book of the Covenant.

cards.text: And Josiah isn't done. He stands by the pillar and makes a covenant before the LORD.

cards.question: Standing by the pillar, what does King Josiah promise in his covenant before the LORD?

answers.text: To follow the LORD and keep His commandments
To rebuild the walls around every city
To send priests out to every nation

cards.question: After making the covenant, what does Josiah have everyone in Jerusalem and Benjamin do?

answers.text: Take a stand in agreement to it
Bring a gift to the house of the LORD
Fast and pray for three whole days

cards.text: So all the people of Jerusalem carry out the covenant of God. Then Josiah removes all the abominations from all the lands belonging to the Israelites, and he requires everyone in Israel to serve the LORD their God.

cards.question: Throughout Josiah's reign, the people turned aside from following the LORD.

cards.text: That's where we set this batch out to cool. Stick with me, friend, because King Josiah's story isn't over.

findings.problem: The card says Josiah is having the house of the LORD repaired. That fact comes from 2 Chronicles 34:8-10 in the passage before this one, not from 34:14. The card cites only 34:14, so the repair fact has no reference.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Card 7 quotes the LORD: "My wrath will be poured out upon this place and will not be quenched." That line rules out the wrong answer "The coming calamity will be called off," so the question becomes a two-way pick.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says "Then Josiah removes all the abominations," which places the removal after the covenant. Verse 33 only says "And Josiah removed..." and gives no order of events. 34:3-7 shows he was already removing idols years earlier.

rule.text: **Times stay true.** No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has 19 cards and only one real joke (card 11). Story cards 1, 3, 7, 14 and 17 are plain narration with no Papa Dorin reaction, comparison or self-deprecation. Moments that could hold a laugh without muddying a fact are passed over: the men going to Huldah, Josiah not being done, and the people taking a stand.

rule.text: Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The closing story card only says the story isn't over and tells no verse. It still cites 2 Chronicles 34:33, which card 18 already asked about and card 17 already told.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, what should its verses field cite: the passage's last verse, the stop's range, or something else?
